collocations.en: to drape a cardigan over one's shoulders
to throw on whatever is at hand
to pull on a jacket and head out

examples.ko: 아침에 급하게 나오느라 아무 셔츠나 걸치고 왔어요.
examples.en: I left in such a rush this morning that I just threw on any old shirt.

examples.ko: 그녀는 잠옷 위에 코트만 걸친 채 택배를 받으러 내려갔다.
examples.en: She went downstairs for the parcel with nothing but a coat thrown over her pajamas.

cloze.sentence: 저녁엔 쌀쌀하니까 뭐라도 하나 {{}} 나가.
cloze.en: It gets chilly in the evening, so throw something on before you go out.

cloze.sentence: 회의실이 추워서 다들 재킷을 어깨에 {{}} 앉아 있었다.
cloze.en: The meeting room was cold, so everyone sat with their jackets draped over their shoulders.

nuance.situation: 셔츠 위에 카디건을 팔을 끼우지 않고 어깨에만 두른 모습을 말하려면? (A cardigan thrown over the shoulders, arms not in the sleeves.)

options.why: Loosely draping or throwing on a garment is 걸치다.
끼다 is for things fitted onto or into a body part: rings, gloves, contact lenses (반지를 끼다). A cardigan isn't one.
쓰다 is for things on the head or face: a hat, glasses, a mask.

collocations.en: on two separate occasions; in two rounds

examples.ko: 이 다리는 10년에 걸친 공사 끝에 지난달 개통했다.
examples.en: The bridge opened last month after construction that spanned ten years.

examples.ko: 내일은 전국에 걸쳐 비가 오겠고, 남부 지방은 바람도 강하게 불겠습니다.
examples.en: Tomorrow rain is expected across the whole country, with strong winds in the south as well.

cloze.sentence: 회사는 두 차례에 {{}} 공식 사과문을 발표했다.
cloze.en: The company issued an official apology on two separate occasions.

cloze.sentence: 경제 전반에 {{}} 구조 개혁이 필요하다는 목소리가 높다.
cloze.en: There are growing calls for structural reform spanning the entire economy.

nuance.situation: 지난 반세기 동안 이어진 연구를 기사에서 소개하려면? (A news piece about research carried on over the past half-century.)

options.why: A stretch of time that the work covers is N에 걸치다: 반세기에 걸친 연구.
걸리다 (take time) has the time as its subject: 반세기가 걸린 연구, "research that took fifty years". Spanning a period is 에 걸치다.
In the "span" sense 걸치다 takes 에, not 을/를: 반세기에 걸친.

meanings: to perch on the edge of

collocations.en: to perch on the edge of a chair
to prop one's leg over the railing
to leave (something) hanging over the back of a chair

examples.ko: 면접 대기실에서 그는 긴장한 듯 의자 끝에 엉덩이만 걸치고 앉아 있었다.
examples.en: In the interview waiting room he sat perched on the very edge of his chair, clearly nervous.

examples.ko: 빨래를 의자 등받이에 걸쳐 놓지 말고 좀 개어 놔.
examples.en: Don't just leave the laundry hanging over the back of the chair. Fold it.

cloze.sentence: 소파에 제대로 앉지도 못하고 팔걸이에 {{}} 앉아서 밥을 먹었다.
cloze.en: I couldn't even sit on the sofa properly, so I ate perched on the armrest.

nearMiss.hint: 걸터앉다 (one word) paints the same picture, but the cue asks for 걸치다: 걸쳐 앉다.

cloze.sentence: 젖은 수건은 욕조 가장자리에 {{}} 말려.
cloze.en: Hang the wet towel over the edge of the tub to dry.

nuance.situation: 재킷을 의자 등받이 위로 넘겨 늘어뜨려 둔 것을 말하려면? (A jacket left hanging over the back of a chair.)

options.why: Something laid across an edge so it hangs down both sides is 걸치다.
꽂다 means to stick something into a slot or hole: a pin, a flower, a USB drive.
걸리다 is intransitive or passive (재킷이 걸려 있다). It can't take 재킷을 as an object.

mnemonic: 맞추다 makes two things 맞다 (fit): a schedule to a person, a watch to a time, pieces to each other. 맞히다 is only for hitting: 정답을 맞히다, 과녁을 맞히다.

collocations.en: to humor someone; to keep someone happy

examples.ko: 강의는 듣는 사람 눈높이에 맞춰서 해야 해요. 전문 용어만 늘어놓으면 소용없어요.
examples.en: You have to pitch a lecture to your audience's level. Just reeling off jargon is useless.

examples.ko: 출판사는 연말 특수에 맞춰 개정판 출간 일정을 앞당겼다.
examples.en: The publisher moved up the revised edition's release to catch the year-end rush.

examples.ko: 팀장 비위 맞추느라 하루가 다 갔네.
examples.en: The whole day went to keeping the team lead happy.

cloze.sentence: 다들 바쁘니까 회의 시간은 제일 늦게 끝나는 사람 일정에 {{}} 정하죠.
cloze.en: Everyone's busy, so let's set the meeting time to fit whoever finishes latest.

cloze.sentence: 시계를 서울 시간에 {{}} 놓는 걸 깜빡했다.
cloze.en: I forgot to set my watch to Seoul time.

nuance.situation: 기차 출발 시각보다 늦지 않게 역에 도착했다. (Arrived at the station in time for the train.)

options.why: Aligning with a time or schedule is 맞추다.
맞히다 means to hit a target or get an answer right (정답을 맞히다). Fitting to a time is 맞추다.
-을 맞아 means "on the occasion of" (개교 50주년을 맞아). It doesn't mean "in time for".

collocations.en: to check answers (against each other or a key)

examples.ko: 시험 끝나고 친구랑 답을 맞춰 봤는데 세 문제나 다르더라.
examples.en: After the exam I compared answers with a friend, and we differed on three questions.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 미리 말을 맞춘 듯 똑같은 진술을 했다.
examples.en: The two gave identical statements, as if they had gotten their stories straight beforehand.

examples.ko: 흩어진 조각을 하나씩 맞추다 보니 사건의 전모가 드러났다.
examples.en: As the scattered pieces were fit together one by one, the full picture of the case emerged.

cloze.sentence: 카드 명세서와 영수증을 한 장씩 {{}} 보면서 빠진 내역이 없는지 확인했다.
cloze.en: I checked the receipts against the card statement one by one to make sure nothing was missing.

cloze.sentence: 천 피스짜리 퍼즐을 주말 내내 {{}} 겨우 완성했다.
cloze.en: I spent the whole weekend putting together a 1,000-piece puzzle and only just finished it.

nuance.situation: 시험이 끝난 뒤 친구와 서로 쓴 답이 같은지 확인했다. (After the exam, you checked whether your answers matched your friend's.)

options.why: Laying two things side by side to see if they line up is 맞추다 (맞춰 보다).
맞히다 is getting a question right, or trying to guess the answer. It doesn't mean comparing.
고치다 means to correct or change. You compared the answers; you didn't change them.

collocations.en: to have rings made (e.g. matching rings)
to order matching T-shirts for a group

examples.ko: 결혼식 때 입으려고 처음으로 양복을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I had a suit tailored for the first time, to wear at the wedding.

examples.ko: 시력이 떨어져서 안경을 새로 맞춰야 할 것 같아.
examples.en: My eyesight's gotten worse. I think I need to get new glasses made.

cloze.sentence: 축제 때 입을 단체 티셔츠를 인쇄소에 {{}} 놨어.
cloze.en: I've put in an order at the print shop for group T-shirts for the festival.

cloze.sentence: 엄마 환갑 선물로 금반지를 하나 {{}} 드렸다.
cloze.en: For Mom's sixtieth birthday, I had a gold ring made for her.

nuance.situation: 기성복이 몸에 안 맞아서 치수를 재고 새로 만들게 했다. (Off-the-rack didn't fit, so you had one made to your measurements.)

options.why: Having something made to order is 맞추다 (맞춤 양복).
맞히다 means to hit or guess correctly. It has nothing to do with tailoring.
고치다 is altering or repairing a suit you already have, not having a new one made.

collocations.en: to disappoint expectations; to go against what was hoped for

examples.ko: 부모님의 기대에 어긋나는 선택이었지만 후회는 없다.
examples.en: It was a choice that went against my parents' expectations, but I have no regrets.

examples.ko: 어른한테 그렇게 말하는 건 예의에 어긋나지.
examples.en: Talking to an elder like that is bad manners.

cloze.sentence: 그 조치는 형평성 원칙에 {{}} 것이어서 거센 비판을 받았다.
cloze.en: The measure ran counter to the principle of fairness and drew fierce criticism.

cloze.sentence: 개인 정보를 동의 없이 공유하는 건 회사 규정에도 {{}}.
cloze.en: Sharing personal data without consent also violates company rules.

nuance.situation: 스포츠 기사: 선수들이 팬들이 바라던 수준의 경기를 보여 주지 못했다. (The team didn't play to the level fans hoped for.)

options.why: Falling short of or running against expectations, rules or manners is N에 어긋나다.
엇갈리다 is for opinions or paths that diverge or cross (평가가 엇갈리다). It doesn't take 기대에.
벗어나다 takes 에서 or 을/를 (기대에서 벗어나다, 예상을 벗어나다). With 에, the verb is 어긋나다.

collocations.en: to miss each other on the way

examples.ko: 서로 마중을 나갔다가 길이 어긋나서 한 시간을 헤맸다.
examples.en: We'd both gone out to meet each other, missed each other on the way, and wandered around for an hour.

examples.ko: 사소한 오해로 시작된 일이었는데 그 뒤로 둘 사이가 자꾸 어긋났어요.
examples.en: It started with a small misunderstanding, but after that things between them kept going wrong.

cloze.sentence: 날씨 때문에 여행 계획이 완전히 {{}} 버렸다.
cloze.en: The weather threw our travel plans completely off.

cloze.sentence: 역 앞에서 만나기로 했는데 출구를 잘못 알아서 길이 {{}} 말았다.
cloze.en: We'd agreed to meet in front of the station, but I had the wrong exit and we ended up missing each other.

nearMiss.hint: 길이 엇갈리다 is just as natural here, but the cue asks for 어긋나다: 길이 어긋나고.

collocations.en: to have the paperwork in order

examples.ko: 이 병원은 최신 장비를 두루 갖추고 있어서 멀리서도 환자들이 찾아온다.
examples.en: This hospital has a full range of the latest equipment, so patients come from far away.

examples.ko: 지원 자격만 갖추면 누구든 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can apply as long as they meet the requirements.

cloze.sentence: 필요한 서류를 다 {{}} 다시 방문해 주세요.
cloze.en: Please come back once you have all the required documents.

cloze.sentence: 중소기업도 기술력을 {{}} 대기업과 충분히 경쟁할 수 있다.
cloze.en: Smaller firms can compete with the big players too, as long as they have the technology.

nuance.situation: 채용 공고: 아래 조건을 충족하는 분을 찾습니다. (A job ad looking for candidates who meet the following.)

options.why: Having qualifications, equipment or documents in place is 갖추다.
차리다 is for setting something out or up (밥상을 차리다, 가게를 차리다, 격식을 차리다). Qualifications aren't set up; you hold them, so it's 갖추다.
거치다 is for stages or procedures you go through (과정을 거치다). Qualifications are something you hold.

examples.ko: 처음 뵙는 자리니까 최소한의 예의는 갖춰야지.
examples.en: It's your first time meeting them, so at least show some basic courtesy.

examples.ko: 시상식장은 정장을 갖춰 입은 참석자들로 가득했다.
examples.en: The awards hall was full of attendees in formal dress.

cloze.sentence: 보고서는 내부용이니까 너무 격식을 {{}} 쓸 필요는 없어요.
cloze.en: The report is for internal use, so there's no need to write it too formally.

nearMiss.hint: 격식을 차리다 is also idiomatic, but the cue asks for 갖추다: 격식을 갖춰.
격식을 차리다 is also idiomatic, but the cue asks for 갖추다: 격식을 갖춰서.

cloze.sentence: 드레스 코드가 있는 자리라서 오랜만에 정장을 {{}} 입고 갔다.
cloze.en: There was a dress code, so for once I went in a proper suit.

collocations.en: to go to Busan via Daejeon
to fly home by way of Hong Kong

examples.ko: 이번 비행기는 도쿄를 거쳐 서울에 도착하니까 환승 시간을 잘 확인하세요.
examples.en: This flight goes via Tokyo before reaching Seoul, so check your connection time carefully.

examples.ko: 이 고서는 여러 수집가의 손을 거쳐 지금의 도서관에 들어오게 되었다.
examples.en: This old book passed through the hands of several collectors before ending up in this library.

cloze.sentence: 이 버스는 시내를 {{}} 공항까지 갑니다.
cloze.en: This bus goes to the airport by way of downtown.

nuance.situation: 서울에서 출발한 열차가 대전역과 대구역에 정차한 뒤 부산에 도착한다. (A train stops at Daejeon and Daegu on its way to Busan.)

options.text: 열차는 대전과 대구를 거쳐 부산에 도착한다.
options.why: Stops along a route are N을 거치다.

options.text: 열차는 대전과 대구를 겪어 부산에 도착한다.
options.why: 겪다 is to go through an experience (hardship, change), not a place.

options.text: 열차는 대전과 대구를 들러서 부산에 도착한다.
options.why: 들르다 takes 에 (대전에 들르다) and means a personal side visit, not scheduled stops on a route.

collocations.en: to go through many twists and turns

examples.ko: 모든 원고는 두 차례의 교정을 거쳐야 인쇄에 들어갈 수 있다.
examples.en: Every manuscript has to go through two rounds of proofreading before it can go to press.

examples.ko: 정식 절차를 안 거치고 일을 처리했다가 나중에 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: We handled it without going through proper procedures, and it became a problem later.

cloze.sentence: 법안은 상임위원회 심사를 {{}} 본회의에 상정되었다.
cloze.en: After standing committee review, the bill was put before the plenary session.

cloze.sentence: 수많은 시행착오를 {{}} 지금의 방식이 자리를 잡았다.
cloze.en: The current method only took hold after a great deal of trial and error.

nuance.situation: 신입 사원은 3개월의 수습 기간을 마쳐야 정식 직원이 된다. (New hires become permanent after a three-month probation.)

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 거쳐 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: A set stage or procedure you pass through is 거치다.

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 겪어 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: 겪다 is for something that happens to you, usually hardship or change (어려움을 겪다). A fixed stage is 거치다.

options.text: 3개월의 수습 기간을 지나쳐 정식 직원이 된다.
options.why: 지나치다 means to go past without stopping, or to overdo something.

collocations.en: to pull up at the door

examples.ko: 건물 앞은 주차 금지라서 뒤쪽 골목에 차를 댔어요.
examples.en: There's no parking in front of the building, so I parked in the alley out back.

examples.ko: 기사님, 저기 편의점 앞에 대 주세요.
examples.en: Driver, could you pull up in front of that convenience store?

cloze.sentence: 비가 오니까 현관 바로 앞에 차를 {{}} 줄게.
cloze.en: It's raining, so I'll pull the car right up to the entrance for you.

cloze.sentence: 주차장이 꽉 차서 차를 어디에 {{}} 할지 모르겠어요.
cloze.en: The lot is full, so I don't know where I'm supposed to park.

examples.ko: 그는 몸이 안 좋다는 핑계를 대고 회식에 빠졌다.
examples.en: He used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip the staff dinner.

examples.ko: 늦은 이유를 대 봐. 납득이 가면 넘어갈게.
examples.en: Go on, tell me why you're late. If it makes sense, I'll let it go.

cloze.sentence: 숙제를 안 해 온 학생들은 저마다 그럴듯한 핑계를 {{}} 바빴다.
cloze.en: The students who hadn't done their homework were all busy coming up with plausible excuses.

cloze.sentence: 근거를 {{}} 못하면 그 주장은 받아들일 수 없어요.
cloze.en: If you can't give any grounds, that claim can't be accepted.

nuance.situation: 늦잠을 자 놓고 버스가 안 와서 늦었다고 했다. (You overslept but blamed the bus.)

options.why: Making an excuse is 핑계를 대다.
들다 takes 예 or 이유 (예를 들다, 이유를 들어 거절하다). With 핑계 the verb is 대다; 핑계를 들다 sounds off.

collocations.en: to lift noodles out (of the water)
to fish out the solids and eat them
to pull a drowning person out

examples.ko: 면이 다 익으면 체로 건져서 찬물에 헹궈 주세요.
examples.en: When the noodles are done, lift them out with a strainer and rinse them in cold water.

examples.ko: 강에 떨어뜨린 휴대폰을 낚시꾼이 그물로 건져 줬다.
examples.en: A fisherman fished out the phone I'd dropped in the river with his net.

cloze.sentence: 국물은 남기고 건더기만 {{}} 먹었다.
cloze.en: I left the broth and fished out just the solids to eat.

nuance.situation: 끓는 냄비에서 삶은 달걀을 국자로 꺼냈다. (You lifted the boiled eggs out of the pot with a ladle.)

options.why: Lifting something solid out of liquid is 건지다.
건네다 means to hand something over to someone.
거르다 means to strain or filter a liquid (or to skip a meal). Lifting solids out one by one is 건지다.

collocations.en: to break even; to get one's money back
to get one good photo out of it

examples.ko: 여행 내내 비만 왔지만 그래도 마음에 드는 사진 몇 장은 건졌어.
examples.en: It rained the whole trip, but I still got a few photos I like out of it.

examples.ko: 사고 차량은 크게 부서졌지만 운전자는 기적적으로 목숨을 건졌다.
examples.en: The car was badly wrecked, but the driver miraculously escaped with his life.

cloze.sentence: 주식으로 손해만 보다가 겨우 본전을 {{}} 바로 다 팔았다.
cloze.en: After nothing but losses on stocks, I finally got back to break-even and sold everything right away.

cloze.sentence: 세 시간짜리 세미나였는데 솔직히 {{}} 게 하나도 없었어.
cloze.en: It was a three-hour seminar, and honestly I didn't get a single thing out of it.

nuance.situation: 투자금을 다 잃을 뻔했는데 겨우 원금만은 되찾았다. (You nearly lost everything but got your principal back.)

options.why: Salvaging something from a loss is 건지다 (본전을 건지다).
견디다 means to endure or hold out. It doesn't mean getting money back.
거르다 means to strain or filter, or to skip (a meal).

meanings: to wear (on the fingers or hands)
to put on (a ring, gloves, lenses)

collocations.en: to fold one's arms; to link arms

examples.ko: 결혼반지를 끼고 설거지하다가 하수구에 빠뜨릴 뻔했어.
examples.en: I was doing the dishes with my wedding ring on and nearly lost it down the drain.

examples.ko: 그는 팔짱을 낀 채 아무 말 없이 회의 내용을 듣고만 있었다.
examples.en: He sat with his arms folded, just listening to the meeting without a word.

cloze.sentence: 손이 시려서 장갑을 두 겹이나 {{}} 나왔다.
cloze.en: My hands were freezing, so I came out wearing two pairs of gloves.

cloze.sentence: 눈이 너무 건조해서 렌즈를 {{}} 수가 없어.
cloze.en: My eyes are so dry I can't put my contacts in.

nuance.situation: 추운 날 손을 보호하려고 장갑을 착용했다. (You put on gloves on a cold day.)

options.why: Things you slip your fingers or hands into take 끼다.
쓰다 is for things on the head or face: hats, glasses, masks.
차다 is for things strapped or hung on: a watch, a belt.

examples.ko: 새벽에 안개가 짙게 끼어서 고속도로에서 사고가 잇따랐다.
examples.en: Thick fog set in before dawn, and there was a string of accidents on the expressway.

examples.ko: 오래 안 쓴 키보드라 자판 사이에 먼지가 잔뜩 꼈네.
examples.en: This keyboard hasn't been used in ages. There's dust packed between all the keys.

cloze.sentence: 하늘에 구름이 잔뜩 {{}} 있어서 별이 하나도 안 보였다.
cloze.en: The sky was so overcast that not a single star was visible.

cloze.sentence: 물때가 {{}} 욕실 타일을 주말에 박박 닦았다.
cloze.en: Over the weekend I gave the bathroom tiles, crusted with soap scum, a hard scrub.

nuance.situation: 아침 일찍 창밖을 보니 온 동네가 뿌옇게 보였다. (Early morning: the whole neighborhood looks hazy.)

options.why: Fog, cloud, dust and grime take 끼다: they form and settle over something.
묻다 is for a liquid or powder getting on something (옷에 잉크가 묻다). Fog doesn't 묻다.

examples.ko: 십 년 넘게 준비한 끝에 그녀는 마침내 자기 책을 내겠다는 꿈을 이뤘다.
examples.en: After more than ten years of preparation, she finally realized her dream of publishing her own book.

examples.ko: 양측은 밤샘 협상 끝에 극적으로 합의를 이루었다.
examples.en: After all-night negotiations, the two sides dramatically reached an agreement.

cloze.sentence: 올해 세운 목표를 다 {{}} 못했지만 절반은 해냈다.
cloze.en: I didn't achieve every goal I set this year, but I got halfway.

cloze.sentence: 작은 목표라도 하나씩 {{}} 가다 보면 자신감이 붙는다.
cloze.en: If you keep achieving goals one at a time, however small, your confidence builds.

nuance.situation: 오랜 노력 끝에 바라던 것을 손에 넣었다. (After long effort, you got what you'd hoped for.)

options.why: Achieving a dream or goal is 이루다, with an object.
이르다 (이르러, 이르렀다) means to reach a point and takes 에: 결론에 이르다.
거두다 goes with results and wins (성과를 거두다, 승리를 거두다), not dreams.

examples.ko: 붉은 단풍이 파란 하늘과 선명한 대조를 이루었다.
examples.en: The red autumn leaves stood out vividly against the blue sky.

examples.ko: 새 휴대폰 출시일에 매장 앞은 아침부터 장사진을 이뤘다.
examples.en: On the new phone's launch day, a long line formed outside the store from early morning.

cloze.sentence: 이 도시는 오래된 한옥과 현대식 건물이 묘한 조화를 {{}} 있다.
cloze.en: In this city, old hanok and modern buildings sit together in a curious harmony.

cloze.sentence: 그 시절 문단의 주류를 {{}} 것은 참여 문학이었다.
cloze.en: What made up the literary mainstream in those days was socially engaged literature.

mnemonic: 빌다 (wish, beg) → 빌어, 빕니다. 빌리다 (borrow) → 빌려. The extra 리 is what you borrow.

collocations.en: to pray for the soul of the departed

examples.ko: 새해 첫날 해돋이를 보면서 가족들 건강을 빌었어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, watching the sunrise, I prayed for my family's health.

examples.ko: 면접 잘 보고 와. 행운을 빌게!
examples.en: Good luck at the interview. I'll keep my fingers crossed!

examples.ko: 고인의 명복을 빕니다.
examples.en: May the departed rest in peace.

cloze.sentence: 합격 발표 날, 어머니는 아침부터 두 손을 모으고 {{}} 계셨다.
cloze.en: On the day the results came out, my mother sat with her hands clasped in prayer from the morning on.

cloze.sentence: 다들 시험 잘 보길 {{}}.
cloze.en: I hope you all do well on the exam.

nearMiss.hint: Spelled 빌게: -(으)ㄹ게 is written with ㄱ.

nuance.situation: 친구의 앞날에 행운이 있기를 바란다. (You wish your friend luck.)

options.why: Wishing or praying is 빌다 → 빌어.
빌려 comes from 빌리다 (borrow). Wishing is 빌다 → 빌어.
-(으)러 means "in order to" and needs a verb of motion after it (빌러 가다).

examples.ko: 약속을 또 어겨서 여자 친구한테 싹싹 빌었어.
examples.en: I broke my promise again, so I groveled to my girlfriend.

examples.ko: 그는 피해자 가족 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 용서를 빌었다.
examples.en: He knelt before the victim's family and begged their forgiveness.

cloze.sentence: 이제 와서 잘못했다고 {{}} 봐야 이미 늦었어.
cloze.en: There's no point begging forgiveness now. It's too late.

nearMiss.hint: 빌려 is from 빌리다 (borrow). Begging is 빌다 → 빌어.

cloze.sentence: 아이는 다시는 안 그러겠다며 엄마에게 {{}}.
cloze.en: The child begged his mother's forgiveness, promising never to do it again.

collocations.en: (I'd like to) take this opportunity to

examples.ko: 이 자리를 빌려 그동안 도와주신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.
examples.en: I'd like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who has helped along the way.

examples.ko: 한 평론가의 말을 빌리자면, 이 소설은 '실패한 걸작'이다.
examples.en: To borrow one critic's words, this novel is a "failed masterpiece."

examples.ko: 평소엔 말도 못 붙이더니 술기운을 빌려 고백을 했다.
examples.en: He'd never even managed to talk to her, but with a little Dutch courage he confessed.

cloze.sentence: 작가는 수상 소감에서 이 자리를 {{}} 번역가에게 고마움을 전했다.
cloze.en: In her acceptance speech, the author took the opportunity to thank her translator.

cloze.sentence: 어느 시인의 표현을 {{}} 그 시절 우리는 '눈부시게 가난했다.'
cloze.en: To borrow a poet's phrase, in those days we were "dazzlingly poor."

mnemonic: Granting a request is the single word 들어주다. "Listen to (someone)" is 듣다 + -어 주다 and is spaced in careful writing: 얘기를 들어 주다.

collocations.en: to give in to a demand

examples.ko: 웬만한 부탁은 다 들어주는데 돈 빌려 달라는 건 좀 곤란해.
examples.en: I'll do you most favors, but lending money is a bit much.

examples.ko: 회사는 결국 노조의 요구를 일부 들어주기로 했다.
examples.en: The company finally agreed to meet some of the union's demands.

cloze.sentence: 아이가 하도 졸라서 강아지를 키우고 싶다는 소원을 {{}} 수밖에 없었다.
cloze.en: My kid begged so much that I had no choice but to grant her wish for a puppy.

cloze.sentence: 그렇게 무리한 요구를 다 {{}} 계약할 이유는 없다.
cloze.en: There's no reason to sign if it means giving in to such unreasonable demands.

nuance.situation: 친구가 이삿짐 나르는 걸 도와 달라고 해서 도와주기로 했다. (A friend asked for help moving, and you agreed.)

options.why: Granting a request is 들어주다, written as one word.
들려주다 means to tell or play something so someone hears it (이야기를 들려주다).
들어 보다 is just hearing the request out. It doesn't say you agreed.

examples.ko: 예약 없이 찾아온 손님들을 그냥 돌려보낼 수밖에 없었다.
examples.en: We had no choice but to turn away the guests who showed up without a reservation.

examples.ko: 멀리서 왔는데 빈손으로 돌려보내기가 미안해서 차라도 한잔 대접했어요.
examples.en: They'd come a long way and I felt bad sending them off empty-handed, so I at least offered them some tea.

cloze.sentence: 주문한 것과 다른 색이 와서 상품을 판매자에게 {{}} 했다.
cloze.en: The wrong color arrived, so I had to send the item back to the seller.

cloze.sentence: 서류 하나 빠졌다고 민원인을 그냥 {{}} 건 너무하잖아요.
cloze.en: Sending someone away just because one document was missing is a bit much.

nuance.situation: 청탁성 선물이 배달되자 그는 뜯지도 않고 보낸 사람에게 다시 보냈다. (A gift that came with strings attached arrived; he sent it back unopened.)

options.why: Sending something or someone back where it came from is 돌려보내다.
내보내다 means to send or let out of a space, to dismiss, or to broadcast. It doesn't mean returning to the sender.
되돌아가다 is intransitive (go back). It can't take 선물을 as an object.

collocations.en: to put one's house on the market
to bring out a new product

examples.ko: 이사 가려고 지난달에 집을 내놨는데 아직 보러 오는 사람이 없네.
examples.en: We put the house on the market last month to move, but nobody's come to see it yet.

examples.ko: 업체는 기존 모델보다 가격을 낮춘 보급형 제품을 내놓았다.
examples.en: The company brought out a budget model priced below its existing line.

cloze.sentence: 오래 몰던 차를 중고 시장에 {{}} 일주일 만에 팔렸다.
cloze.en: I put the car I'd driven for years on the used market, and it sold within a week.

cloze.sentence: 그 출판사는 해마다 번역 시리즈를 꾸준히 {{}} 있다.
cloze.en: That publisher has been steadily bringing out a translation series every year.

nuance.situation: 회사가 새 스마트폰 모델을 출시했다. (A company launched a new smartphone model.)

options.why: Bringing a product out onto the market is 내놓다.
꺼내다 means to take something out of a container, or to bring up a topic.
내보내다 means to send people or things out of a place, or to air a broadcast.

meanings: to come up with (measures, a plan)

collocations.en: to issue a statement of position

examples.ko: 정부는 전세 사기 피해자를 위한 지원책을 내놓았다.
examples.en: The government put forward support measures for victims of jeonse fraud.

examples.ko: 회의는 세 시간이나 했는데 아무도 뾰족한 수를 못 내놓더라.
examples.en: The meeting went on for three hours, and nobody could come up with a real solution.

cloze.sentence: 논란이 커지자 구단은 공식 입장을 {{}} 사태 수습에 나섰다.
cloze.en: As the controversy grew, the club issued an official statement and set about damage control.

cloze.sentence: 비판만 하지 말고 대안을 {{}} 봐.
cloze.en: Don't just criticize. Come up with an alternative.

nuance.situation: 전문가 위원회가 문제를 해결할 방법을 제시했다. (An expert committee proposed a way to solve the problem.)

options.why: Putting forward plans, measures or statements is 내놓다.
내리다 goes with decisions, conclusions and orders (결론을 내리다). Proposals are 내놓다 or 제시하다.

mnemonic: 건들다 is the accepted short form: 건들지 마.

collocations.en: to mess with other people's things

examples.ko: 내 책상 위 서류는 순서대로 놔둔 거니까 건드리지 마.
examples.en: The papers on my desk are in order, so don't touch them.

examples.ko: 고양이가 자고 있을 때 건드리면 할퀼 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you poke the cat while it's sleeping, it might scratch you.

cloze.sentence: 전시품은 손으로 {{}} 마시고 눈으로만 감상해 주세요.
cloze.en: Please don't touch the exhibits. Look only.

cloze.sentence: 설정을 잘못 {{}} 프로그램이 아예 안 켜진다.
cloze.en: I messed with the settings and now the program won't even start.

examples.ko: 괜히 실직 얘기를 꺼내서 친구 아픈 데를 건드린 것 같아.
examples.en: I think I touched a sore spot by bringing up my friend's job loss for no reason.

examples.ko: 그의 한마디가 동료들의 자존심을 건드렸다.
examples.en: His one remark wounded his colleagues' pride.

cloze.sentence: 그 사람 지금 예민하니까 괜히 {{}} 말고 가만히 있어.
cloze.en: He's touchy right now, so don't go provoking him. Just leave it.

cloze.sentence: 기자의 질문이 감독의 신경을 {{}} 듯했다.
cloze.en: The reporter's question seemed to get on the coach's nerves.

nuance.situation: 농담으로 한 말인데 상대가 몹시 불쾌해했다. 상대의 자부심을 상하게 한 것이다. (A joke offended someone's sense of pride.)

options.why: Hurting someone's pride or touching a nerve is 건드리다.
자존심을 걸다 means to stake one's own pride on something.
자존심을 세우다 means to stand on (or protect) one's pride, the opposite of wounding it.

collocations.en: to look back on the past
to take a hard look at oneself

examples.ko: 한 해를 돌아보니 바쁘기만 했지 남은 게 별로 없네.
examples.en: Looking back on the year, I was busy the whole time but don't have much to show for it.

examples.ko: 남을 탓하기 전에 먼저 자신을 돌아볼 필요가 있다.
examples.en: Before blaming others, you need to take a look at yourself.

cloze.sentence: 누가 부르는 것 같아서 뒤를 {{}} 아무도 없었다.
cloze.en: I thought someone called my name, but when I looked back there was no one there.

cloze.sentence: 이번 실패를 계기로 그동안의 운영 방식을 차분히 {{}} 한다.
cloze.en: We should use this failure as a chance to take a calm look back at how we've been running things.

nuance.situation: 졸업식 날, 지난 4년간의 대학 생활을 떠올리며 생각에 잠겼다. (On graduation day, you thought back over four years of college.)

options.why: Looking back over a stretch of the past is 돌아보다.
둘러보다 means to look around a place (매장을 둘러보다). A stretch of past time is 돌아보다.

collocations.en: to take a walk around the neighborhood

examples.ko: 장관은 태풍 피해 지역을 돌아보며 복구 상황을 점검했다.
examples.en: The minister toured the typhoon-hit areas, checking on recovery progress.

examples.ko: 이사 갈 동네를 미리 한 바퀴 돌아봤는데 생각보다 조용하더라.
examples.en: I took a walk around the neighborhood we're moving to, and it's quieter than I thought.

cloze.sentence: 시장은 취임 첫날 공사 현장 여러 곳을 직접 {{}}.
cloze.en: On her first day in office, the mayor personally toured several construction sites.

cloze.sentence: 경비원은 밤 열 시가 되면 층마다 한 바퀴씩 {{}} 문이 잠겼는지 확인한다.
cloze.en: At ten every night the security guard makes a round of each floor, checking that the doors are locked.

mnemonic: 돌아보다 here is 돌아다니며 보다: you move from place to place and check (현장을 돌아보다, 순찰하듯 돌아보다). 둘러보다 is looking around one place or browsing (매장을 둘러보다).

collocations.en: to make fun of the way someone talks

examples.ko: 어릴 때 이름이 특이하다고 친구들이 많이 놀렸어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my friends teased me a lot because my name was unusual.

examples.ko: 남의 발음을 놀리는 건 장난이라도 상처가 될 수 있다.
examples.en: Mocking someone's pronunciation can hurt, even as a joke.

cloze.sentence: 형이 겁쟁이라고 하도 {{}} 울음을 터뜨렸다.
cloze.en: My older brother teased me so much for being a scaredy-cat that I burst into tears.

cloze.sentence: 장난으로 한 말인데, {{}} 것처럼 들렸다면 미안해.
cloze.en: I only meant it as a joke, but I'm sorry if it sounded like I was making fun of you.

nuance.situation: 친구가 넘어진 걸 보고 다른 친구들이 웃으며 장난스럽게 흉내를 냈다. (Friends laughed and mimicked a friend who'd tripped.)

options.why: Making fun of someone is 놀리다.
노리다 means to aim at or watch for (a target, a chance).
놀다 means to play or hang out (with someone).

examples.ko: 주문이 끊겨서 공장 설비 절반을 몇 달째 놀리고 있다.
examples.en: Orders dried up, so half the factory's equipment has been sitting idle for months.

examples.ko: 시골에 놀리는 밭이 있는데 주말농장으로 써 볼까 해.
examples.en: We've got a field sitting unused in the countryside. I'm thinking of using it as a weekend farm.

cloze.sentence: 빈방을 그냥 {{}} 아까우니까 서재로 쓰자.
cloze.en: It's a waste to leave the spare room unused, so let's make it a study.

cloze.sentence: 비싼 장비를 {{}} 두는 대신 다른 팀에 빌려주기로 했다.
cloze.en: Instead of leaving the expensive equipment sitting idle, we decided to lend it to another team.

collocations.en: to bring something up; to start to say something
to take out of a wallet

examples.ko: 헤어지자는 말을 어떻게 꺼내야 할지 며칠째 고민 중이야.
examples.en: I've been agonizing for days over how to bring up breaking up.

examples.ko: 그는 한참 망설이다가 어렵게 이야기를 꺼냈다.
examples.en: After hesitating for a long while, he finally raised the subject.

cloze.sentence: 연봉 얘기를 먼저 {{}} 게 좀 눈치 보여서 가만히 있었어.
cloze.en: I felt awkward bringing up salary first, so I kept quiet.

cloze.sentence: 회의 막바지에 누군가 예산 문제를 {{}} 분위기가 싸해졌다.
cloze.en: Toward the end of the meeting someone raised the budget issue, and the mood went cold.

nuance.situation: 회식 자리에서 결혼 계획 이야기를 처음으로 했다. (At a staff dinner, you brought up your wedding plans for the first time.)

options.why: Bringing up a topic in conversation is 꺼내다.
들추다 is to dig up something hidden or past, usually embarrassing (과거를 들추다).
내리다 goes with decisions and conclusions (결론을 내리다), not topics.

meanings: to let go of (a desire, a burden)

collocations.en: to let go of one's ambitions
to let go; to stop worrying
to step down from a position

examples.ko: 결과는 내가 어쩔 수 없는 거니까 이제 마음을 내려놓기로 했어.
examples.en: The result is out of my hands, so I've decided to stop worrying about it.

examples.ko: 그는 30년간 지켜 온 대표직을 내려놓고 고향으로 돌아갔다.
examples.en: He stepped down from the CEO post he'd held for 30 years and went back to his hometown.

cloze.sentence: 완벽하게 하겠다는 욕심을 {{}} 오히려 일이 잘 풀렸다.
cloze.en: Once I let go of the urge to do it perfectly, things actually went more smoothly.

cloze.sentence: 무거운 장바구니를 현관에 {{}} 한숨 돌렸다.
cloze.en: I set the heavy shopping bags down in the entryway and caught my breath.

nuance.situation: 그동안의 집착을 버리고 편해지기로 했다. (You decided to stop clinging and be at peace.)

options.why: Letting go of something on purpose is 내려놓다.
놓치다 is to miss or lose hold of something by accident (기회를 놓치다).
떨어뜨리다 means to drop something, or to lower a figure (성적을 떨어뜨리다).

collocations.en: to be left off the list

examples.ko: 이번 회식은 사정이 있어서 빠질게요.
examples.en: Something's come up, so I'll sit out this staff dinner.

examples.ko: 최종 명단에서 내 이름이 빠져 있어서 담당자에게 다시 확인했다.

nearMiss.hint: 들려서 is from 들리다 (be heard). "Drop by" is 들르다 → 들러서, 들렀다.

cloze.sentence: 오늘 회사 앞 카페에 {{}} 네 생각이 나서 쿠키 샀어.
cloze.en: I stopped by the café in front of the office today, thought of you, and bought you a cookie.

nearMiss.hint: 들렸는데 is from 들리다 (be heard). "Stop by" is 들르다 → 들렀는데.

nuance.situation: 퇴근하면서 잠깐 서점에 갔다 왔다. (On the way home you popped into a bookstore.)

options.why: 들르다 drops its 으: 들러, 들렀다.
들렸다 is from 들리다 (be heard, be lifted). It's a very common misspelling of 들렀다.
거치다 treats the place as a waypoint on a route. For a quick personal visit, 들르다 is the natural verb.

mnemonic: Tie → 매다: 매듭 (a knot) starts with 매. Everything slung over a shoulder is 메다.
meanings: to carry on one's shoulder or back
to sling (a bag) over one's shoulder

collocations.en: to carry a bag on one's shoulder or back
to take the lead on something risky

examples.ko: 노트북 때문에 백팩을 메고 다녔더니 어깨가 뻐근해요.
examples.en: I've been carrying a backpack because of my laptop, and my shoulders are stiff.

examples.ko: 아무도 나서지 않자 결국 막내가 총대를 메고 팀장에게 건의했다.
examples.en: When nobody would step up, the youngest finally took one for the team and raised it with the team lead.

cloze.sentence: 등산객들은 무거운 배낭을 {{}} 산길을 올랐다.
cloze.en: The hikers climbed the trail with heavy packs on their backs.

nearMiss.hint: 매다 means to tie (넥타이를 매다, 신발 끈을 매다). Bags on the shoulder or back take 메다: 메고.

cloze.sentence: 가방을 한쪽 어깨에만 {{}} 자세가 나빠진다.
cloze.en: If you carry your bag on just one shoulder, your posture suffers.

nearMiss.hint: 매다 means to tie. Carrying on the shoulder is 메다: 메면.

nuance.situation: 학생이 책가방을 등에 지고 학교에 갔다. (A student went to school with a schoolbag on her back.)

options.why: Bags carried on the shoulder or back take 메다.
매다 means to tie (a tie, shoelaces, a knot). It's a very common misspelling here.
옆구리에 끼다 means to tuck under one's arm. On the back, it's 메다.

collocations.en: to be too choked up to go on
to feel one's heart tighten (with grief)

examples.ko: 수상 소감을 말하다가 목이 메어서 잠시 말을 멈췄다.
examples.en: Partway through her acceptance speech she got choked up and had to pause.

examples.ko: 엄마 편지를 읽는데 목이 메어서 끝까지 못 읽겠더라.
examples.en: I was reading Mom's letter and got so choked up I couldn't finish it.

cloze.sentence: 아들의 이름을 부르던 아버지는 목이 {{}} 더 말을 잇지 못했다.
cloze.en: Calling out his son's name, the father choked up and couldn't go on.

nearMiss.hint: A common but nonstandard form. 메다 → 메어: 목이 메어.
매이다 means to be tied. Choking up is 메다 → 메어.

cloze.sentence: 고구마를 물도 없이 먹었더니 목이 {{}} 혼났네.
cloze.en: I ate sweet potato without any water and it got stuck in my throat. Awful.

nuance.situation: 졸업식에서 은사님께 감사 인사를 하다가 울컥했다. (Thanking your old teacher at graduation, you were overcome.)

options.why: Choking up is 목이 메다 → 메어.
매다 means to tie. Choking up is 메다.
막다 is transitive (block something). The intransitive is 막히다: 목이 막히다.

collocations.en: not think of it in time
not get a chance to grab or take care of

examples.ko: 네가 그렇게 힘들었는지 미처 몰랐어. 미안해.
examples.en: I didn't realize you were having such a hard time. I'm sorry.

examples.ko: 급하게 나오느라 우산을 미처 챙기지 못했다.
examples.en: I left in such a hurry that I didn't get a chance to grab an umbrella.

cloze.sentence: 차가 너무 빨리 달려와서 {{}} 피할 겨를도 없었다.
cloze.en: The car came at us so fast there wasn't even time to get out of the way.
cloze.cue: ㅁㅊ · (not) in time; always with a negative

cloze.sentence: 회의 자료에 오류가 있는 줄 {{}} 모르고 그대로 배포했다.
cloze.en: We distributed the meeting materials without having caught the error in time.

nuance.situation: 약속 시간이 바뀌었다는 문자가 늦게 와서 알지 못했다. (The text about the time change came late, so you didn't know.)

options.why: 미처 + a negative: something didn't happen in time (미처 몰랐다, 미처 못 챙겼다).
차마 is "couldn't bring oneself to" and goes with a held-back action (차마 말을 못 했다), not with not knowing.
미리 means "beforehand" and goes with things done ahead of time (미리 알려 주다). Not knowing in time is 미처.

mnemonic: 왠지 is the only 왠: it's 왜인지 squeezed. Everything else is 웬: 웬일, 웬만하다, 웬걸.

collocations.en: to feel uneasy for no clear reason

examples.ko: 처음 와 본 동네인데 왠지 낯설지 않았다.
examples.en: It was my first time in that neighborhood, yet somehow it didn't feel strange.

examples.ko: 오늘은 왠지 일이 잘 풀릴 것 같은 예감이 들어.
examples.en: I've got a feeling things are going to go well today, somehow.

cloze.sentence: 별일 없을 텐데 {{}} 자꾸 마음이 불안하다.
cloze.en: Nothing's probably wrong, but for some reason I keep feeling uneasy.

nearMiss.hint: 왠지 = 왜인지 ("why" + -ㄴ지). 웬 is "what sort of" (웬일, 웬 떡).

cloze.sentence: 그 사람 목소리가 {{}} 모르게 익숙했다.
cloze.en: There was something oddly familiar about his voice.

nearMiss.hint: 왠지 = 왜인지 ("why" + -ㄴ지). 웬 is "what sort of" (웬일, 웬 떡).

nuance.situation: 특별한 이유는 없는데 기분이 좋다. (You're in a good mood for no particular reason.)

options.why: 왠지 (from 왜인지) means "somehow, for some reason".
Misspelling. 웬 means "what sort of" (웬일이야?). "Somehow" is 왠지.
웬일 is a noun, "what's the occasion?" (웬일이야?). It can't modify the sentence like this.

collocations.en: to have been just about to

examples.ko: 안 그래도 너한테 전화하려던 참이었는데 마침 잘 왔다.
examples.en: I was just about to call you. Perfect timing.

examples.ko: 우산이 없어 난감하던 차에 마침 동료가 지나가다 씌워 주었다.
examples.en: I was stuck without an umbrella when, as luck would have it, a colleague walked by and shared hers.

cloze.sentence: 배가 고프던 참에 {{}} 친구가 떡볶이를 사 왔다.
cloze.en: Just when I was getting hungry, my friend showed up with tteokbokki.
cloze.cue: ㅁㅊ · just then, as it happens

cloze.sentence: 다음 주에 서울 간다고? {{}} 잘됐다, 부탁할 게 있었거든.
cloze.en: You're going to Seoul next week? Perfect. I had a favor to ask.

nuance.situation: 그 문제를 상의하려던 참에 그 사람이 딱 그때 사무실에 들어왔다. (Right as you meant to raise the issue, he walked in.)

options.why: 마침 is timing that happens to fit: "just then, as it happens".
마침내 means "finally, at long last", after a long wait or effort.
비로소 means "only then", after some condition was met.

collocations.en: this just isn't going to work
all things considered, it's better to

examples.ko: 아무래도 오늘 안에는 다 못 끝낼 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm afraid I won't be able to finish it all today.

examples.ko: 날씨가 이래서는 아무래도 야외 행사는 취소해야겠다.
examples.en: With the weather like this, it looks like we'll have to cancel the outdoor event.

cloze.sentence: 열이 계속 나는 걸 보니 {{}} 병원에 가 봐야 할 것 같아.
cloze.en: Since the fever won't go down, I think I'd better see a doctor after all.
cloze.cue: ㅇㅁㄹㄷ · all things considered (+ a guess)

cloze.sentence: 이 정도 예산으로는 {{}} 무리겠어요.
cloze.en: On a budget like this, I'm afraid it's just not doable.

nuance.situation: 여러 가지를 따져 보니 결국 이번 여행은 못 갈 것 같다. (Weighing everything, it looks like you can't make the trip.)

options.why: 아무래도 leads into a reluctant conclusion: "all things considered, I'm afraid …".
아무리 needs a concessive ending: 아무리 -아도/-더라도 ("no matter how …").
아무렇게나 means "carelessly, any old way".

collocations.en: to pull it off in the end
to go ahead and do it anyway

examples.ko: 말렸는데도 동생은 기어이 그 비싼 카메라를 사고야 말았다.
examples.en: We tried to talk him out of it, but my brother went ahead and bought that expensive camera anyway.

examples.ko: 괜찮다는데도 기어이 집 앞까지 데려다주더라.
examples.en: I said it was fine, but he insisted on walking me all the way home.

cloze.sentence: 비 오는 날 등산은 위험하다고 그렇게 말렸는데 {{}} 가더니 감기에 걸려 왔다.
cloze.en: We begged him not to go hiking in the rain, but he went anyway and came back with a cold.

cloze.sentence: 몇 번이나 떨어졌지만 그녀는 {{}} 꿈을 이뤘다.
cloze.en: She failed several times, but in the end she made her dream come true.
cloze.cue: ㄱㅇㅇ · in the end, no matter what

nuance.situation: 가족들이 다 반대했는데도 그는 결국 회사를 그만두었다. (The whole family objected, but he quit his job anyway.)

options.why: 기어이 is doing something in the end despite resistance or obstacles.
기껏 sets up a letdown: "after all that effort, only to …" (기껏 준비했더니 취소됐다).
기왕 means "since (it's already so)" and needs a follow-up clause (기왕 그만둔 거, 푹 쉬어).

examples.ko: 한참 동안 서류를 넘기던 면접관이 이윽고 고개를 들었다.
examples.en: After leafing through the papers for a long while, the interviewer at length looked up.

examples.ko: 긴 침묵이 흐른 뒤, 그녀가 이윽고 입을 열었다.
examples.en: After a long silence, she finally spoke.

cloze.sentence: 밤새 내리던 눈이 그치고 {{}} 동쪽 하늘이 밝아 오기 시작했다.
cloze.en: The snow that had fallen all night stopped, and before long the eastern sky began to brighten.

cloze.sentence: 멀리서 기차 소리가 들리더니 {{}} 열차가 승강장으로 들어왔다.
cloze.en: We heard a train in the distance, and presently it pulled into the platform.

nuance.situation: 소설 속 장면: 한참 망설이던 주인공이 잠시 뒤 말을 꺼냈다. (In a novel, the hero hesitates, then speaks after a moment.)

options.why: 이윽고 narrates the next thing that happens after a pause: "presently, at length".
이따가 means "in a little while (from now)" and is for plans, not past narration.
이미 means "already": he had spoken before, not after the pause.

meanings: (but) when it actually comes to it

examples.ko: 다들 걱정하는데 정작 본인은 태평하네.
examples.en: Everyone's worried, but the person in question is completely relaxed.

examples.ko: 몇 달을 준비했는데 정작 발표 당일엔 머릿속이 하얘졌다.
examples.en: I prepared for months, but on the actual day of the presentation my mind went blank.

cloze.sentence: 우산을 늘 들고 다니다가 {{}} 비 오는 날엔 놓고 나왔다.
cloze.en: I always carry an umbrella, but on the one day it actually rained I left it at home.

cloze.sentence: 말은 많았지만 {{}} 중요한 문제는 아무도 언급하지 않았다.
cloze.en: There was a lot of talk, but nobody mentioned the issue that actually mattered.

nuance.situation: 주변 사람들은 모두 그의 건강을 걱정하는데 그 사람만 아무렇지 않아 한다. (Everyone worries about his health except him.)

options.why: 정작 singles out the key person or thing against expectations: "the one actually concerned".
과연 means "as expected" or "really?". It doesn't mark a contrast with everyone else.
하물며 means "let alone, all the more" and needs an a fortiori comparison.

accepted: when it actually comes to it

collocations.en: there's no need to go that far
strictly speaking; if you insist on splitting hairs

examples.ko: 택시 타면 금방인데 굳이 마중 나올 필요 없어.
examples.en: It's quick by taxi, so there's no need to bother coming to pick me up.

examples.ko: 굳이 따지자면 이번 일은 우리 쪽 책임이 더 크다.
examples.en: Strictly speaking, we bear more of the responsibility for this.

cloze.sentence: 다 아는 얘기를 {{}} 또 설명할 필요는 없잖아요.
cloze.en: There's no need to go out of your way to explain what everyone already knows.
cloze.cue: ㄱㅇ · go to the trouble of
